long_biography.plain_text:
Encouraged by performer Dennis Sheridan, Greg Meyer took singing lessons with Wally Carr and began securing professional engagements at hotels and clubs. He later opened for George Benson and performed at jazz festivals in France. Singing became a continuing part of his working life alongside his business ventures.

At BASK Gili Meno, the Indonesian resort he founded, Meyer applied lessons from his own travels. He wanted restaurant food that matched Australian dining standards. He worked with architect Gary Fell and creative director George Gorrow to combine modern design with the setting of a tropical island.
long_biography.html:
Encouraged by performer Dennis Sheridan, Greg Meyer took singing lessons with Wally Carr and began securing professional engagements at hotels and clubs. He later opened for George Benson and performed at jazz festivals in France. Singing became a continuing part of his working life alongside his business ventures.

At BASK Gili Meno, the Indonesian resort he founded, Meyer applied lessons from his own travels. He wanted restaurant food that matched Australian dining standards. He worked with architect Gary Fell and creative director George Gorrow to combine modern design with the setting of a tropical island.

confidence.reason: Direct personal interview supports training, performances and collaboration; subsequent music coverage corroborates sustained singing, while a separate interview explains his guest-led restaurant standards.
